slicekit init

Adds the kit to a repository. Run it once at the repository root; running it again is safe.

Usage
slicekit init --shape <backend|fullstack|data> [--name <n>] [--docs <dir>] [--cli <command>] [--default-branch <name>] [--test <cmd>] [--lint <cmd>] [--build <cmd>] [--e2e <cmd>] [--protect]

It writes .slicekit/config.json, the docs layout, the Claude Code commands, agents and hooks, the git hooks (it sets core.hooksPath to .githooks) and the CI workflow when there is none yet. It prints created, updated or skipped for each file, then hooks run: <cli>. An existing config wins, so --shape is then optional.

  • --shape <backend|fullstack|data>: the project's shape; it decides which files are rendered. fullstack adds the designer agent. Required unless a config exists.
  • --name <n>: the program name. Default: the folder's name.
  • --docs <dir>: the docs root. Default: docs.
  • --cli <command>: how the hooks and the workflow run the kit. Default: node node_modules/slicekit/bin/slicekit.js with a local install, else slicekit. Init warns when the command does not answer --version.
  • --default-branch <name>: the default branch of a new config. Without it, init takes the branch origin's HEAD points at, else the first of main, master and git's init.defaultBranch that is a local branch.
  • --test, --lint, --build, --e2e <cmd>: the team's commands. CI runs one job per declared command. No defaults.
  • --protect: after the files are written, sets on the git host each rule the default branch lacks, as one ruleset named slicekit: a pull request before merge, one approving review, the kit's CI checks required, and force push refused. It needs admin rights on the repository. It is the only place where the kit changes a host setting. It prints set <branch>: <rule> per rule, or host rules: <branch> has every rule; nothing set.
What it reads and writes

Reads the repository, an existing config and, with --protect, the git host's rulesets. Writes the config, the docs layout, .claude/, .githooks/, the workflow file, the rendered copies under .slicekit/rendered/ and git's core.hooksPath. It commits nothing. With --protect it writes one ruleset on the host.

Exit codes
  • 0done; warnings go to stderr
  • 1--protect: the git host refused or could not be reached; the files are already written
  • 2bad usage, not run from the repository root, no --shape and no config, or a config problem, including a flag that disagrees with the existing config
Example
$ npm install --save-dev slicekit
$ npx slicekit init --shape backend --name orders --test "npm test" --lint "npm run lint"
created .slicekit/config.json
…
hooks run: node node_modules/slicekit/bin/slicekit.js

Back to the guide

slicekit instructions

Prints an agent's brief or a slash command's procedure. The rules of every agent and command live here, not in a prompt.

Usage
slicekit instructions <role> [P<n>/S-<nn>] [--worktree <path> | --summary]slicekit instructions --command <name> [args...]

The first form prints an agent's brief: its rules, the slice file's summary, the cited requirements and decisions, the team's commands, the writing rules and the slice's tasks. Roles: developer, reviewer, fixer, auditor, ops, designer. Without a slice ID it takes the slice from the current branch.

  • --worktree <path>: the worktree the agent works in; the brief's Where section names it.
  • --summary: the short form of the brief, which the subagent-start hook injects. It takes no --worktree.

The second form prints a slash command's procedure. --command must come first; the name is one of intake, specify, gaps, plan, build, review, release, ops, audit. Everything after the name is passed to the procedure unparsed.

Each slash command file runs the second form and follows what it prints; see the slash commands.

What it reads and writes

Reads the config, the templates the kit ships, the slice file, the spec, the decisions and the current branch. It writes nothing.

Exit codes
  • 0printed
  • 1a template the kit does not ship
  • 2bad usage, an unknown role, an unknown command name, an argument that is not a slice address, or a config problem
Example
$ slicekit instructions developer P1/S-02 --worktree .worktrees/P1-S-02
# Brief: developer
…
$ slicekit instructions --command review 19
# /slicekit review
…

Back to the guide

slicekit intake

The steps of /slicekit intake that the CLI takes: freeze the source document, then record each interview question and its answer.

Usage
slicekit intake snapshot <file|url> [--slug <s>] [--who <w>]slicekit intake ask --pass <product|platform> --topic <t> --question <q>slicekit intake answer (--answer <a> [--type <T>] | --open --why <w> --recommendation <r>) [--who <w>] [--interface <name> [--source <file>:<line>]]slicekit intake done
SubcommandWhat it does
intake snapshot <file|url>Copies the source, a file or a URL of at most 50 MB, to <docsRoot>/intake/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.<ext> beside a sidecar that pins its SHA-256, and commits both. The snapshot is frozen from then on. --slug names the file; --who says who supplied it.
intake askRecords the question the agent is about to ask and prints question <n>. --pass is product or platform; --topic and --question are required. It refuses a new question while the last has no answer row, and a product question once the platform pass has started.
intake answerWrites one row to <docsRoot>/decisions.md for the question just asked and prints its ID. --answer <a> with an optional --type (Decision, Information, Action, Counsel), or --open --why <w> --recommendation <r> when the person could not answer. --interface <name> marks an interface.
intake doneCommits decisions.md, platform.md and observability.md, then prints one open: <D-ID> <question> line per open row, or open: none. It refuses while a question has no answer, while a pass asked nothing, or when a spec file appeared or changed during the interview.
What it reads and writes

Reads the source document and the interview session file. Writes the snapshot and its sidecar under <docsRoot>/intake/, rows in <docsRoot>/decisions.md, and two commits: the snapshot's and the answers'.

Exit codes
  • 0done; snapshot prints the path, answer the D-ID
  • 1refused: a protected branch, a failed fetch, a question with no answer, a file problem
  • 2bad usage or bad input: no such file, a bad slug, a URL with a password, a source over the size cap
Example
$ slicekit intake snapshot ./brief/orders.md
docs/intake/2026-10-31-orders.md
$ slicekit intake ask --pass product --topic=users --question="Who places an order?"
question 2
$ slicekit intake answer --answer="Shop staff, and customers on the web store"
D-02
$ slicekit intake done
open: D-09 Which payment provider do refunds go through?

Back to the guide

slicekit journal

Verifies or prints the session journal, and records the journal heads after a merge.

Usage
slicekit journal verify [--against <ref>]  | journal show [-n 10] [--branch <b>]  | journal heads <merge sha>

The session-end hook appends one line per session to this clone's journal file for the current branch. Each file is a hash chain.

journal verify checks each file's hash chain, that the journal directory holds no unexpected entry, and that no committed journal file was shortened or removed since the merge base. It prints journal: <n> lines in <m> files verified, journal: no entries, or every problem. It never writes.

  • --against <ref>: the ref whose merge base the shortening check uses. Default: the default branch.

journal show prints the last lines of this clone's journal file for one branch.

  • -n <count>: how many lines. Default: 10.
  • --branch <b>: which branch's file. Default: the current branch.

journal heads <merge sha> is a step of the CI sync job. It appends to .slicekit/journal-heads.log one line per journal file whose last hash changed at that merge: the file, its last hash, the merge commit, and the run ID, workflow and actor of the CI run. It prints journal heads: <n> lines for <sha7>. check --ci recomputes each line; see the journal rule.

What it reads and writes

verify and show read the journal files and git, and write nothing. heads reads git and the variables GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_WORKFLOW and GITHUB_ACTOR, and appends to .slicekit/journal-heads.log.

Exit codes
  • 0verified, printed, or the heads lines appended
  • 1verify: at least one problem, each printed. heads: the sha is not a commit of this clone
  • 2bad usage; show: -n is not a positive whole number; heads: not one commit sha, or not in a CI run
Example
$ slicekit journal verify
journal: 42 lines in 6 files verified
$ slicekit journal show -n 1 --branch slice/P1-S-02-place-order

Back to the guide

slicekit ops

The two steps of /slicekit ops that the CLI takes: what the ops agent is handed for a symptom, and the check of the report it replies with.

Usage
slicekit ops context <symptom> [--path <p>]… [--json]slicekit ops check <report>

ops context <symptom> prints the report path on its first line, then symptom:, one file: line per file the symptom's words match, the history of those files as history prints it, the runbook, observability.md and the last release record. The words of a symptom typed without quotes are one symptom.

A word is a run of three or more letters and digits. It names each file one of whose path segments equals it. A word that matches more than fifty files is printed on a too broad: line and names none. A word that matches no file is printed on a no file: line.

  • --path <p>: also takes the files history would match for this path. It may be given several times.
  • --json: prints one JSON document.

ops check <report> prints ok <report>, or one <report>:<line> <message> line per problem:

  • a missing or empty section among ## Likely slices and pull requests, ## First checks and ## Proposed actions;
  • a slice or pull request named in the first section that the graph does not hold;
  • a <file>:<line> cited in First checks that is not a line of a file in the repository;
  • a proposed action not marked by who may take it: (anyone), (on-call) or (owner: <name>). A section that proposes nothing is the one line None.;
  • a missing Skipped: or Not checked: closing line.
What it reads and writes

Reads the graph file and files of the repository. ops context creates the empty report file .slicekit/reports/ops-<k>.md, which the ignore rules that init writes cover. Neither runs git, calls the host, takes an action or changes a tracked file.

Exit codes
  • 0context: printed. check: the report has no problem
  • 1context: the symptom names no file in the graph. check: at least one problem. Either: no graph, or a graph of an older schema
  • 2bad usage, a missing symptom, a --path that is not in the graph, a report path that is not a file, or a config problem
Example
$ slicekit ops context "checkout returns 502" --path src/orders/
.slicekit/reports/ops-1.md
symptom: checkout returns 502
file: src/orders/place.js
history:
P1/S-02  PR #14  APPROVE  unreleased
runbook: docs/runbook.md
observability: docs/observability.md
last release: none
$ slicekit ops check .slicekit/reports/ops-1.md
ok .slicekit/reports/ops-1.md

Back to the guide

slicekit plan

Says whether planning may start.

Usage
slicekit plan check

plan check prints ready to plan, or one blocker per line: each clarification marker as <file>:<line> clarification marker: …, then the first earlier stage, up to the gap scan, that is not done. It is step 2 of /slicekit plan.

What it reads and writes

Reads the spec, the decisions, the gaps file and the intake sidecars. It writes nothing.

Exit codes
  • 0ready
  • 1blockers, one per line
  • 2bad usage or a config problem
Example
$ slicekit plan check
ready to plan

Back to the guide

slicekit pr

Commits, pushes and opens or updates a document pull request.

Usage
slicekit pr open --title <t> --body-file <f> [--commit <message> --paths <a,b>] [--draft] [--base <b>]

pr open optionally commits the named paths, pushes the current branch and opens its pull request through the git host. When one is already open for the branch, it updates that pull request's body instead. It never pushes a protected branch. It is the last step of specify, gaps, plan and release; slice pull requests use build pr.

  • --title <t>: the pull request title. Required.
  • --body-file <f>: a UTF-8 file holding the body. Required.
  • --commit <message> and --paths <a,b>: commit these comma-separated paths with this message. The two go together.
  • --draft: opens the pull request as a draft.
  • --base <b>: the branch it merges into. Default: the default branch.
What it reads and writes

Reads the body file, the config and git. Writes one commit when --commit is given, pushes the branch, and opens or updates the pull request on the git host.

Exit codes
  • 0prints #<n> <url>, or updated #<n> <url>
  • 1git, the host or the body rules refused
  • 2bad usage, or a body file that cannot be read or is not UTF-8
Example
$ slicekit pr open --title "[spec] orders" --body-file /tmp/spec-body.md \
    --commit "docs(spec): orders" --paths docs/spec,docs/decisions.md
#12 https://github.com/acme/orders/pull/12

Back to the guide

slicekit ready-label

Decides whether a slice pull request gets the ready label, and sets it. The generated workflow runs it.

Usage
slicekit ready-label

Ready means: the title names a slice, SLICEKIT_CHECKS_OK=true, the latest verdict on the current head has no open blocker, and neither has the latest independent verdict, unless review.independent on the base branch makes that review optional. It prints the decision and its reason. With GH_TOKEN set it adds or removes the label, creating it when needed.

The label is information. Merging stays a person's act.

What it reads and writes

Reads the pull request from GITHUB_EVENT_PATH, the base from GITHUB_BASE_REF, the state files and the verdicts. With GH_TOKEN it writes the label on the git host.

Exit codes
  • 0always, even on bad usage or a failed label call, which becomes a GitHub warning
Example
$ SLICEKIT_CHECKS_OK=true slicekit ready-label
ready-label: P1/S-02 not ready: independent review missing
ready-label: GH_TOKEN not set; label left unchanged

Back to the guide

slicekit release

Writes a phase's release record and sets its slices released. It commits nothing and deploys nothing.

Usage
slicekit release P<n> [--dry-run | --undo]

It writes the record <docsRoot>/releases/P<n>.md, sets each slice of the phase released and rewrites BUILD.md. It prints the record's path, then one released <slice> line per slice. pr open then commits the three and opens the [release] P<n> pull request; merging that pull request is the release.

It refuses, with one line per reason and nothing written:

  • a slice that is not merged;
  • a slice with no recorded pull request;
  • a slice that says runbook: yes and neither changed a section of the runbook nor gave a Runbook line that begins "no operational change";
  • a record that already exists;
  • a run that is not on a release/<slug> branch at the tip of the default branch.

Options:

  • --dry-run: prints the record it would write, and writes nothing but the migration of an older config. It runs on any branch.
  • --undo: releases nothing. It removes a record that is not committed, puts the phase's state files and BUILD.md back as the last commit has them, and prints removed <record>. It refuses a record the last commit holds, and when there is no record. It cannot be given with --dry-run.
What it reads and writes

Reads the phase's slice files and state files, the runbook, git and the git host's pull requests. Writes the release record, the state files of the phase and BUILD.md.

Exit codes
  • 0the record written, printed (--dry-run) or removed (--undo)
  • 1refused, one line per reason; or a git or git host error
  • 2bad usage, both flags, an argument that is not a phase, or a config problem
Example
$ slicekit release P1 --dry-run
$ slicekit branch release p1
release/p1
$ slicekit release P1
docs/releases/P1.md
released P1/S-01
released P1/S-02

Back to the guide

slicekit review

Checks out a pull request's head for an independent review.

Usage
slicekit review start <PR>

review start <PR> checks out the pull request's head in a fresh worktree, .worktrees/review-P<n>-S-<nn>, on slice/P<n>-S-<nn>-review, which pushes to the slice branch. It prints four lines: slice, worktree, round and verdict.

It refuses a pull request that is not open, not a slice pull request or from a fork, and a review worktree with uncommitted changes. A refusal that the head is not origin/<branch> can be a push the git host has not seen yet: try once more after a minute.

It is step 2 of /slicekit review. The later steps use build subcommands with --worktree <wt>.

What it reads and writes

Reads the pull request from the git host, the state file and git. Fetches, and creates the review worktree and its branch.

Exit codes
  • 0ready to review
  • 1refused
  • 2the pull request number is not a positive whole number, or a config problem
Example
$ slicekit review start 14
slice P1/S-02
worktree C:/work/orders/.worktrees/review-P1-S-02
round 2
verdict C:/work/orders/P1-S-02-r2.md

Back to the guide

slicekit shipped

Prints a phase's release record.

Usage
slicekit shipped P<n> [--json]

It prints the record's path, the requirements the phase delivered and its pull requests with their URLs. Release records come from release. For a phase with no record it answers P<n> has no release record and exits 1.

  • --json: prints one JSON document, also on an error.
What it reads and writes

Reads only .slicekit/graph/graph.json. It runs no git and calls no host. It writes nothing.

Exit codes
  • 0answered
  • 1no graph, a graph of an older schema, or a phase with no release record
  • 2bad usage, a phase the graph does not hold, or a config problem
Example
$ slicekit shipped P1
slicekit: P1 has no release record

Back to the guide

slicekit spec

Checks that every requirement and interface in the spec is grounded.

Usage
slicekit spec verify

spec verify checks what the spec stands on: the earlier stages are done, every requirement cites a decision row or an intake file that exists, and every interface named at intake has a contract. It lists clarification markers but does not count them as findings. /slicekit specify runs it after the spec files are written, until it exits 0.

What it reads and writes

Reads the spec files, the contracts, the decisions and the intake files. It writes nothing.

Exit codes
  • 0prints the counts, then each clarification marker
  • 1one <file>:<line> <message> line per finding
  • 2bad usage or a config problem
Example
$ slicekit spec verify
spec verified: 18 REQ, 2 contracts, 1 clarification markers
docs/spec/refunds.md:22 [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: who approves a refund over the limit?]

Back to the guide

slicekit stage

Checks, from the files, that a stage and every stage before it are complete.

Usage
slicekit stage require <stage>

The stages, in order: intake, clarify, specify, spec-review, gap-scan, stack, plan, build, release. On success stage require <stage> prints ready: <stage>. Otherwise it prints the first blocker and the command that clears it on stderr, followed by pending items that do not block.

It is the gate at the start of specify (clarify), gaps (spec-review) and build (plan). Type it to see where the program stands.

What it reads and writes

Reads the intake sidecars, the decisions, the spec, the gaps file, the phase and slice files and the state files. It writes nothing.

Exit codes
  • 0ready
  • 1a blocker
  • 2bad usage, an unknown stage, or a config problem
Example
$ slicekit stage require plan
gap scan not done: docs/spec/gaps.md has no Scanned: line; gaps scan has not run; run /slicekit gaps

Back to the guide

slicekit state

Reads or writes one slice's state file. The build commands call it; a person types it rarely.

Usage
slicekit state set <id> <to> [--commit sha] [--test-exit n] [--check-exit n] [--tests a,b] [--pr-number n --pr-title t --pr-url u --pr-sha s] [--verdict path --round n --blockers n [--independent]] [--ci-status s --ci-sha s] [--merged-at iso] [--release path] [--backfill]slicekit state show <id> [--json]slicekit state unfreeze <id> <path>

The states, in order: todo, tests-red, building, draft-pr, in-review, changes-requested, ci-green, ready, merged, released.

state set <id> <to> is the only writer of a slice's state file. It checks the move's precondition against the evidence passed and refuses otherwise. It prints <id> <state>.

EvidenceWhat it records
--commit <sha>the commit the move rests on
--test-exit <n>, --check-exit <n>the exit codes of the test command and of check
--tests <a,b>the test files, for tests-red
--pr-number, --pr-title, --pr-url, --pr-shathe pull request and its head
--verdict <path>, --round <n>, --blockers <n>, --independenta review verdict, its round, its open blockers, and whether it is independent
--ci-status <s>, --ci-sha <s>the CI result and the head it ran on
--merged-at <iso>the merge time
--release <path>the release record, for released
--backfillwith merged: takes the merge time and head from the git host, to record a merge that happened outside the loop

state show <id> prints <id> <state> PR <#n|->. With --json it prints the whole state file: history, frozen tests, verdicts, handoff.

state unfreeze <id> <path> releases one test frozen at tests-red and records it in the history. build amend is the usual way: it also requires the slice file to record the amendment.

What it reads and writes

Reads the slice file and the state file under .slicekit/state/; --backfill reads the git host. set and unfreeze write the state file under a lock. show writes nothing.

Exit codes
  • 0moved, printed or unfrozen
  • 1set: refused: <reason>, or a git host error. unfreeze: the path is not a frozen test of the slice
  • 2bad usage, an unknown state or slice, a held lock, or a config problem
Example
$ slicekit state show P1/S-03
P1/S-03  ready  PR #17
$ slicekit state set P1/S-03 merged --backfill --pr-number 17
P1/S-03  merged

Back to the guide

slicekit status

Lists every slice's state, syncs merges from the git host and regenerates BUILD.md.

Usage
slicekit status [--json] [--write] [--sync]

With no option it lists every slice as <id> <state> PR <#n|-> <name>.

  • --sync: first asks the git host which pull requests merged and moves those slices, from draft-pr to ready, to merged.
  • --write: regenerates the generated region of BUILD.md from the slice files and the state files, and prints BUILD.md updated or unchanged in place of the list.
  • --json: prints one JSON document: stage, slices, synced, warnings, build.

After a merge to the default branch, the sync job of the generated workflow runs status --sync --write, then sync open puts the change up as a pull request.

What it reads and writes

Reads the slice files, the state files and, with --sync, the git host. --sync writes state files; --write writes BUILD.md. It commits nothing.

Exit codes
  • 0done
  • 2a bad config or slice file, a git host error, a held lock, or bad usage
Example
$ slicekit status --sync
synced P1/S-02 → merged (PR #14)
P1/S-01  merged  PR #11  Health check
P1/S-02  merged  PR #14  Place an order
P1/S-03  todo  PR -  Refunds

Back to the guide

slicekit sync

Opens the pull request that carries the state change after a merge. The CI sync job runs it; a person does not type it.

Usage
slicekit sync open

sync open is the sync job's last step, after status --sync --write and journal heads on the default branch. It puts the change on a sync/<short sha> branch, opens a pull request titled [sync] state after <short sha> through the git host, and starts the workflow on that branch so its checks run. The job never pushes to the default branch.

What it prints:

OutputMeaning
#<n> <url>, then dispatched <workflow> on <branch>it opened the pull request
sync: #<n> <url> is already open for <branch>, then the dispatched linethat pull request was open; no second one is opened
sync: no state change; nothing to openthe merge changed no state
sync: #<n> … cut from a later merge, already carries this state; nothing to opena newer sync pull request holds this change
closed #<n>: superseded by #<m>an older sync pull request was closed, since the new one carries every change it did

A person approves and merges the sync pull request. On it, check --ci runs the sync-release and journal rules. The sync job needs the repository setting that lets GitHub Actions create pull requests; the host-rules rule reports it when it is off.

What it reads and writes

Reads the working tree's changes and git. Writes one commit on a new sync/<short sha> branch, pushes it, opens the pull request, closes superseded ones and dispatches the workflow, all through the git host.

Exit codes
  • 0opened one, found one open, or had nothing to open
  • 1git, the git host or the body rules refused
  • 2bad usage or a config problem
Example
$ slicekit sync open
#161 https://github.com/acme/orders/pull/161
dispatched slicekit.yml on sync/8d2e483

Back to the guide

slicekit trace

Traces a requirement down to its commits and tests, or a file up to its requirements.

Usage
slicekit trace <REQ-…> | trace --file <path> [--json]

For a requirement it prints the tree under it: its slices with their pull requests, commits and files, then the tests that cover it. With --file <path> it prints the tree above a file: the slices whose commits touched it, with the requirements and decisions above each.

  • --json: prints one JSON document, also on an error.

It answers "what delivered this requirement?" and "why does this file exist?"

Reads only .slicekit/graph/graph.json. It runs no git and calls no host. It writes nothing.

  • 1no graph (run slicekit graph), or a graph of an older schema
  • 2bad usage, an ID or path the graph does not hold, or a config problem

requirement REQ-2.8 `/slicekit review <PR>`
  slice P2/S-16 `/slicekit review` and `--parallel` (merged)
    pull request #19 https://github.com/adityapandya1/agentic-slicekit/pull/19
    commit af5e0d7 ci: the kit's own jobs get 60 minutes
      file .github/workflows/slicekit.yml
…

slicekit uncovered

Lists untested requirements, unlinked tests and commits outside a slice.

Usage
slicekit uncovered [--json]

It prints three lists: requirements no test covers, test files that name no requirement, and commits on the default branch with no Slice: trailer, merge commits left out.

  • --json: prints one JSON document, also on an error.

Run it before a release, or to find work done outside the loop.

What it reads and writes

Reads only .slicekit/graph/graph.json. It runs no git and calls no host. It writes nothing.

Exit codes
  • 0answered
  • 1no graph (run slicekit graph), or a graph of an older schema
  • 2bad usage, an ID or path the graph does not hold, or a config problem

  REQ-3.2 …

slicekit update

Compares the files the kit renders with what the installed version would write, and updates them.

Usage
slicekit update [--yes] [--check] [--force]

It prints each file that differs, with a status and a diff. Without --yes it writes nothing. Only the managed block of a file is re-rendered; text a team added outside it is kept.

StatusMeaning
changedthe kit ships a newer template
missingthe file is not there
driftedsomeone edited the managed block by hand

Options:

  • --yes: writes the files whose status is changed or missing.
  • --check: writes nothing; exits 1 when any file is drifted or missing.
  • --force: with --yes, also overwrites drifted files.

Run it after upgrading the slicekit package. The managed rule of check reports the same drift.

What it reads and writes

Reads the config, the kit's templates, the rendered files and their reference copies under .slicekit/rendered/. With --yes it writes the rendered files and the reference copies.

Exit codes
  • 0done, or a dry run
  • 1with --check, a file drifted or is missing; with --yes, a drifted file was left in place
  • 2bad usage or a config problem
Example
$ npx slicekit update
changed .claude/commands/slicekit-build.md
…
run again with --yes to apply
$ npx slicekit update --yes

Back to the guide

slicekit visualize

Shows the graph as one self-contained page.

Usage
slicekit visualize [--port <n>] [--write <file>]

By default it serves the page and the graph file on 127.0.0.1 only, prints the URL, opens nothing, and runs until Ctrl-C.

  • --port <n>: the port, 0 to 65535. Default: 0, any free port.
  • --write <file>: writes the page to a file instead of serving it, and prints its path.
What it reads and writes

Reads .slicekit/graph/graph.json. With --write it writes the one file named.

Exit codes
  • 0written, or served and stopped
  • 1no graph, or the file cannot be written or its folder does not exist
  • 2both options, a bad port, bad usage or a config problem
Example
$ slicekit visualize --write graph.html
graph.html

Back to the guide

slicekit workflow

Prints, writes or checks the GitHub Actions workflow that the config renders.

Usage
slicekit workflow [--write | --check]

The workflow holds a gate job, a job per team command, a job per observability step, the ready label and the sync job that runs after a merge. With no option it prints the workflow.

  • --write: writes .github/workflows/slicekit.yml. It warns when the test command never reads SLICEKIT_SHARD, since it then runs whole in every shard.
  • --check: compares that file with the render.

Run it after changing the team commands or the CI settings in the config. The generated workflow runs workflow --check on every pull request.

What it reads and writes

Reads the config, observability.md and the action pins in templates/workflow/pins.json. With --write it writes the workflow file.

Exit codes
  • 0printed, written, or matching
  • 1with --check, the file is missing or differs from the render
  • 2both flags, bad usage or a config problem
Example
$ slicekit workflow --write
updated .github/workflows/slicekit.yml

Back to the guide

Check rules

ci-body

Check rule

Under --ci, the pull request's body carries the sections the kit requires.

A blocking rule: any finding fails check. It is one of the rules of slicekit check, and a finding is printed as ci-body <file>:<line> <message>.

What fails
  • A slice pull request whose body lacks one of the nine sections: Done when, Proof, Decisions, Runbook, Infra / migration, Try it, Reviewer blocked, Should-haves declined, Skipped / not checked.
  • A section that appears twice, is out of order or is empty.
  • A body with no ## [P<n>/S-<nn>] <name> heading naming the slice of the title: pull request body heading does not name <slice>.
  • A [spec], [plan], [sync] or [release] pull request whose body lacks Done when, Proof or Decisions; the other six sections are not asked of it.
When it judges

Only under check --ci, and only when the GitHub event holds a pull request. A pull request opened by an actor listed in ci.botActors is exempt. pr open and build pr refuse the same bodies before they push.

How to clear a finding

Open slice pull requests with build pr --notes <file>, which builds the body. For a document pull request, write the three sections into the body file given to pr open.

The failure it prevents

A pull request reaches review with no proof of what was run, no steps to try it and no word on what was skipped, so the reviewer and the person who merges cannot tell what the slice claims or what nobody checked.

ci-title

Check rule

Under --ci, the pull request's title begins with the slice it delivers, and that slice was opened through the build loop.

A blocking rule: any finding fails check. It is one of the rules of slicekit check, and a finding is printed as ci-title <file>:<line> <message>.

What fails
  • title must begin with [P<n>/S-<nn>].
  • slice <id> has no slice file, or has no state file.
  • slice <id> is <state>; open the pull request through /slicekit build: the slice is before draft-pr, so the pull request was opened by hand.
  • slice <id> is <state>; a change after merge needs its own slice: the slice is merged or released.
  • a [sync] title belongs to a sync/<short sha> branch: a [sync] title on any other branch.
When it judges

Only under check --ci, and only when the GitHub event holds a pull request. A title that begins [spec] , [plan] or [release] is exempt, and so is [sync] on a sync branch. Draft and closed pull requests are judged alike. A pull request opened by an actor listed in ci.botActors is exempt.

How to clear a finding

Open the pull request with build pr. For a change to a slice that already merged, plan a new slice.

The failure it prevents

A pull request opened by hand skips the red tests, the frozen tests and the recorded verdicts, and once it merges no state file or graph edge links its commits to a slice or a requirement.

citations

Check rule

Every requirement cites a source that exists, every slice file names requirements and decisions that exist, and no ID is defined twice.

A blocking rule: any finding fails check. It is one of the rules of slicekit check, and a finding is printed as citations <file>:<line> <message>.

What fails
  • A requirement heading at a level other than ## or ###.
  • A requirement whose Cites: line names no decision row and no intake file that exists.
  • A slice file that names a requirement or a decision that does not exist, or that cannot be read.
  • A test of a slice's evaluation set that covers no requirement.
  • A decision or requirement ID defined twice: duplicate id <id> (<file>:<line> and <file>:<line>).
  • On a slice branch, a test file the branch adds or modifies that names no REQ ID: test file names no requirement.
When it judges

On every run. The test-file part judges only a slice branch, against its merge base with the default branch; deleted files and the default branch itself are not judged.

How to clear a finding

Add the Cites: line or correct the ID. Name the REQ ID a test covers in the test file, in a comment or a test name.

The failure it prevents

A requirement appears in the spec with nothing behind it, so nobody can say who asked for it or why, and a test exists that covers no requirement, so the graph cannot say what the test proves.

commands

Check rule

Every command the team declared in the config can be found on this machine.

A blocking rule: any finding fails check. It is one of the rules of slicekit check, and a finding is printed as commands <file>:<line> <message>.

What fails
  • commands.<name>: "<word>" not found on PATH or under node_modules/.bin, for test, lint, build and e2e.
  • A local settings file that is tracked by git: it holds one machine's settings and would change every clone's test command.
  • A local settings file that cannot be read.
When it judges

On every run. Nothing is executed. The command is split on &&, ||, ; and the pipe sign outside quotes; in each part the leading NAME=value words are skipped and the first word is looked up, unless it is a shell builtin such as cd, export or echo. A word with a path separator must be a file. An empty command means "not declared" and is not a finding. Outside CI the test command judged is the local one when a local settings file sets it; check --ci judges the committed command.

How to clear a finding

Install the tool, or correct the command in .slicekit/config.json and commit it with build config.

The failure it prevents

A typo in the test command, or a tool that is not installed, makes every build step and CI job fail at its first run, long after the config was written, with an error that does not point back at the config.

coverage

Check rule

Once a program is planned, every requirement belongs to a slice and every slice can be built and judged.

A blocking rule: any finding fails check. It is one of the rules of slicekit check, and a finding is printed as coverage <file>:<line> <message>.

What fails
  • <REQ> is named by no slice.
  • slice <id> lists no expected changes.
  • slice <id> has no happy test, or no negative test.
  • A phase's Order line that misses a group, repeats one or names a group no slice has; or a phase with more than one Order line.
  • slices <a> and <b> in <step> both expect <path>: two slices that run at the same time expect to change one path.
  • A state file that is not valid JSON.
When it judges

On every run once the program is at the plan stage or any slice is past todo. Four shared roots are never an overlap: the repository root ., anything under test/, src/cli/index.js and the runbook.

How to clear a finding

Correct the plan files: name the requirement in a slice, add the missing test row, or put two slices that change one file in groups of different Order steps. Then run status --write.

The failure it prevents

A requirement is planned into no slice and is never built, or two slices built side by side change the same file and the second one to merge overwrites or conflicts with the first.

frozen

Check rule

On a slice branch, a test of the evaluation set stays as it was at the red commit.

A blocking rule: any finding fails check. It is one of the rules of slicekit check, and a finding is printed as frozen <file>:<line> <message>.

What fails
  • frozen test changed after red: <path>.
  • red commit <sha> of <slice> is not in this repository.
  • state file <path> was removed after it recorded the red commit <sha7>, one finding naming the state file, when the tip holds no state file and an earlier version of it in the tip's history recorded a red commit.
  • A state file that is not valid JSON at the tip, or frozen tests that name a path outside the repository.
When it judges

On a slice branch whose state file records a red commit. The tip judged is HEAD, or under --ci the pull request's head. The state file, the red commit, the slice file and the tests are read from git objects, never the working tree, so a file hidden with assume-unchanged or skip-worktree is judged by its committed content. A tip that has no state file is judged by the versions of the file in the tip's history: the red commit and the frozen tests are read from them, so each frozen test that changed after red is still a finding, beside the one for the removal. A slice whose state file never recorded a red commit gets no finding. A slice file changed in a commit of the slice branch after the red commit lifts the freeze, as build amend does. freezeTests set to false in the config turns the rule off.

How to clear a finding

Restore the test. Restore a removed state file from the last commit that holds it (git revert of the commit that removed it). When the test itself is wrong, a person agrees, the slice file records the amendment, and build amend <id> --test <path> --reason <r> unfreezes it.

The failure it prevents

An agent that cannot make a failing test pass edits the test until it does, and the slice merges green while the behaviour the evaluation set asked for was never built.

hooks

Check rule

The git hooks the kit installs are present, executable and the ones git runs.

A blocking rule: any finding fails check. It is one of the rules of slicekit check, and a finding is printed as hooks <file>:<line> <message>.

What fails
  • core.hooksPath is not set (must be .githooks); run slicekit init.
  • core.hooksPath is <value>, not .githooks.
  • .githooks/<name> is missing; run slicekit init, for each of pre-commit, pre-merge-commit and prepare-commit-msg.
  • .githooks/<name> is not executable.
When it judges

On every run inside a git repository. On Windows there is no mode bit, so a tracked hook's mode in the index is read and an untracked hook is not judged for it.

How to clear a finding

Run slicekit init, or git config core.hooksPath .githooks. For the mode, git update-index --chmod=+x <file>.

The failure it prevents

Git hooks do not survive a clone, so in a fresh clone nothing refuses a commit on the protected branch or adds the slice trailer, and nobody notices until the trailer rule fails in CI.

host-rules

Check rule

The git host's rulesets on the default branch hold every rule the kit relies on.

A blocking rule: any finding fails check. It is one of the rules of slicekit check, and a finding is printed as host-rules <file>:<line> <message>.

What fails
  • a pull request is not required before merge.
  • no approving review is required; with a CODEOWNERS file, the approving review is not required to come from a code owner.
  • the kit's CI checks are not required: <names>: the gate and checks jobs of the generated workflow.
  • force push is not refused.
  • Under --ci: host rules not checked: <why>, when the host cannot be read.
  • Under --ci, when the workflow has a sync job: GitHub Actions may not create pull requests.
When it judges

On every run in a repository with an origin remote. Only rulesets are read; a branch on classic branch protection alone is told to move to a ruleset. Outside CI, a host that cannot be read is a note, host rules not checked, that is printed and does not block; so is the Actions setting when it is off or cannot be read. The rule never writes a host setting.

How to clear a finding

A person with admin rights runs slicekit init --protect, which sets the missing rules as one ruleset named slicekit. The Actions setting is turned on by hand under Settings, Actions, General, Workflow permissions.

The failure it prevents

The default branch accepts a direct push or a merge with red CI, so every check the kit runs on a pull request can be bypassed by anyone with write access, and the kit's gate is advice only.

journal

Check rule

The session journal is an unbroken, append-only record, and under --ci its commits are signed.

A blocking rule: any finding fails check. It is one of the rules of slicekit check, and a finding is printed as journal <file>:<line> <message>.

What fails
  • A journal file whose hash chain is broken, at its first broken line.
  • An entry in the journal directory that is not a *.log file or its *.lock.
  • A journal file committed at the merge base that was shortened or removed.
  • Under --ci: commit <sha7> changes a journal file and its signature is not verified by the host.
  • Under --ci: a change to .slicekit/journal-heads.log on a branch that is not a sync branch, a file that is not the old file plus new lines, or a new line that differs from the line CI computes for its merge commit.
  • Under --ci, on a sync branch: a missing heads line for a journal file the merge changed.
When it judges

On every run when a journal exists. The git part is silent outside a repository. Signatures and CI runs are read only under --ci. The rule never repairs a journal.

How to clear a finding

Restore the journal file from git; never edit one by hand. Sign the commits that change a journal file. The heads file is written only by journal heads in the sync job.

The failure it prevents

Someone edits or deletes the record of what a session did, such as a declined finding or an amended test, and nothing shows the record was changed after the fact.

layout

Check rule

Every file and folder slicekit init lays down is still there, and .claude/ holds no file of another shape.

A blocking rule: any finding fails check. It is one of the rules of slicekit check, and a finding is printed as layout <file>:<line> <message>.

What fails
  • <path> is missing; run slicekit init: a file or a directory of the layout is gone or is the wrong kind.
  • <file> is not part of shape <shape>; run slicekit update: a file under .claude/ that the kit ships only for another shape.
When it judges

On every run once .slicekit/config.json exists. A file under .claude/ that the kit does not ship is the team's and is never a finding.

How to clear a finding

Run slicekit init to put back what is missing, or slicekit update to remove a file of another shape.

The failure it prevents

A deleted or renamed part of the layout, such as the decisions file or the state folder, makes a later command fail in the middle of a build or read an empty folder as "nothing planned".

managed

Check rule

Every file the kit renders still holds the block the kit wrote.

A blocking rule: any finding fails check. It is one of the rules of slicekit check, and a finding is printed as managed <file>:<line> <message>.

What fails
  • <file>: managed block edited since slicekit wrote it; run slicekit update --force or revert.
  • <file>: managed file missing; run slicekit update.
  • <file>: exists but is not managed by slicekit; move it or run slicekit update --force.
  • <file>: no reference copy; cannot tell a kit change from an edit.
When it judges

On every run. The comparison is the one slicekit update makes at the kit's own version. A file whose status is changed, meaning the kit ships a newer template, is not a finding: that is for update to write.

How to clear a finding

Revert the edit, or run slicekit update --yes --force to take the kit's text. Put a team's own rules outside the managed block.

The failure it prevents

Someone weakens a hook command, an agent's tool list or a slash command by editing the rendered file, and every later session runs with the weaker rule while the kit still appears installed.

queue

Check rule

BUILD.md reads exactly as the slice files and their state say.

A blocking rule: any finding fails check. It is one of the rules of slicekit check, and a finding is printed as queue <file>:<line> <message>.

What fails
  • BUILD.md is missing, or has no generated region marker.
  • BUILD.md row for <slice> says "<a>", state says "<b>".
  • BUILD.md row for <slice> has no slice file, or BUILD.md lacks a row for <slice>.
  • BUILD.md is stale: the generated region differs in order, position or a line outside the rows.
When it judges

On every run once a slice file or a state file exists. Only the generated region is compared; the text below the marker is the team's.

How to clear a finding

Run slicekit status --write. Never edit the generated region by hand.

The failure it prevents

The build queue a person reads says a slice is still to do when it is merged, or the reverse, so work is started twice or a release is planned on slices that are not done.

references

Check rule

Every path, anchor and ID a doc names exists.

A ratchet rule: a file fails only when its count of findings is above its baseline; see baseline. It is one of the rules of slicekit check, and a finding is printed as references <file>:<line> <message>.

What fails
  • missing file <path>: a link target, or a path in backticks, that does not exist with exactly that spelling.
  • missing anchor #<anchor> in <file>: a link into a Markdown file that has no such heading.
  • unknown id <id>: a requirement, decision, gap, contract or slice ID that nothing defines.
  • intake file has no valid sidecar.
  • stale pending marker for <slice>; the slice is done, remove it.
When it judges

On every run, over every Markdown file under the docs root, BUILD.md, README.md, the verdicts and the rendered agent files. Text in a fenced code block is not read. A line that carries the example marker, the HTML comment slicekit:example, is skipped. A line that carries a pending marker naming a slice is skipped until that slice is merged. In an unmerged slice file, the paths under Expected changes are promises and are not checked. A frozen intake snapshot is not checked. The rule is a ratchet: each file has a baseline, and only a count above it fails.

How to clear a finding

Correct the path or the ID, or create the file. After fixing findings in a repository that started with some, run slicekit baseline update to lower the baseline.

The failure it prevents

A spec, a runbook or a slice file points at a file that was renamed or a decision that was never recorded, and the person or agent who follows the reference at the moment it matters finds nothing there.

runbook

Check rule

A slice that says it changes operations changes the runbook, or says why not.

A blocking rule: any finding fails check. It is one of the rules of slicekit check, and a finding is printed as runbook <file>:<line> <message>.

What fails
  • runbook: the slice says runbook: yes, <runbook> changed no section, and the Runbook line does not begin "no operational change", reported at the slice file's runbook: line.
When it judges

On a slice branch whose slice file says runbook: yes and whose state is from draft-pr to ready. The pull request body comes from the CI event or from SLICEKIT_PR_BODY; with neither the rule does not judge, because build pr already refuses to open such a pull request. The branch passes when it changes a ## section of the runbook, or when the body's Runbook line begins "no operational change". release applies the same judgement to every runbook: yes slice of the phase.

How to clear a finding

Add or change the runbook section the slice calls for, or give the reason in the notes file: "runbook": "no operational change: <reason>".

The failure it prevents

A slice adds a queue, a migration or an alert and merges with the runbook unchanged, so the person on call meets the new failure with no first check written down.

style

Check rule

No doc uses a phrase from the team's filler list.

A ratchet rule: a file fails only when its count of findings is above its baseline; see baseline. It is one of the rules of slicekit check, and a finding is printed as style <file>:<line> <message>.

What fails
  • banned phrase "<phrase>", at the line where it starts.
  • catalogue missing "<phrase>": the filler list in the config, or a doc section that defines the list, dropped a phrase of the kit's seed list.
When it judges

On every run, over the same docs as references. A phrase is matched as whole words, in any case, across a line break inside a paragraph. Code spans, fenced blocks, link targets and URLs are not read. Inflections are not derived: a team lists each form it bans. The list is style.banned in the config. The rule is a ratchet: each file has a baseline, and only a count above it fails.

How to clear a finding

Rewrite the sentence to state the fact. After removing findings, run slicekit baseline update.

The failure it prevents

Specs, verdicts and runbooks fill with phrases that state no fact, and a reader cannot tell a checked claim from decoration.

sync-release

Check rule

Under --ci on a sync pull request, the version, the changelog and the rendered files are exactly what CI computes for that merge.

A blocking rule: any finding fails check. It is one of the rules of slicekit check, and a finding is printed as sync-release <file>:<line> <message>.

What fails
  • <file> differs from what CI computes for the merge <sha7>, one finding per file. The line's second half says what a sync pull request may change in that file.
  • For a rendered file of an example, that second half is a sync pull request changes an example file only to its fresh render at the version it sets (slicekit update --yes in that folder).
  • the version for the merge <sha7> could not be computed.
When it judges

Only under check --ci, on a sync/<short sha> branch. CI checks out the merge the branch names in a temporary worktree, runs the sync step there and compares. So package.json may change only in its version, CHANGELOG.md only by the one new section, and a rendered file only to its fresh render at that version.

The rule also judges the rendered files of each folder under examples/ that holds a rendered directory and a config. The sync step renders each example at the version it sets, as slicekit update --yes would in that folder, so an example file is accepted only where it equals that render.

The version is the one the sync step computes: the patch number up by one, or the minor number up by one when the merge completes a phase for the first time. A phase whose line a CHANGELOG.md section at the merge holds has had its minor version, so a sync pull request that carries a second minor version for that phase is one finding on package.json and one on CHANGELOG.md.

The rule is silent when the config has no release.auto and the branch changes none of those files.

How to clear a finding

Do not edit a sync pull request by hand. Close it and let the sync job open a new one, or restore the files to what the job wrote.

A finding on an example file means the file on the sync branch is not the render of that example at the version the pull request sets: it was edited on the branch, or it is stamped with another version. Re-run the sync job of that merge, which renders the examples again and replaces the branch. To see the render the rule expects, check out the merge with the version the pull request sets and run slicekit update --yes in that folder.

The failure it prevents

A sync pull request, which a person approves as routine bookkeeping, carries a hand-set version number or an edited rendered hook, and that change ships in the next published version without a slice or a review.

trailer

Check rule

On a slice branch, every commit the branch adds names the slice in a Slice: trailer.

A blocking rule: any finding fails check. It is one of the rules of slicekit check, and a finding is printed as trailer <file>:<line> <message>.

What fails
  • commit <sha7> has no Slice trailer.
  • commit <sha7> names <other>, branch is <slice>.
When it judges

On a slice branch. The commits judged are the first-parent line of the tip, leaving out everything the default branch already holds. A merge commit is exempt, since git writes its message. Under --ci the tip is the pull request's head.

How to clear a finding

Commit through build commit, which adds the trailer; the prepare-commit-msg hook adds it to a commit made by hand on a slice branch.

The failure it prevents

A commit lands on the default branch that belongs to no slice, so trace, history and uncovered cannot say which requirement it serves or whether anyone reviewed it.

workspace

Check rule

A slice names a repository the workspace lists, and a contract names both of its parties.

A blocking rule: any finding fails check. It is one of the rules of slicekit check, and a finding is printed as workspace <file>:<line> <message>.

What fails
  • slice <id> names repo <name>, which <workspace file> does not list, or ; there is no workspace file.
  • <contract> names no producer, or names no consumer.
  • A workspace file that cannot be read.
When it judges

On every run. A slice file's repo: passes when it is . or the name of an entry of the workspace file. A contract's party is a slice address or, for one outside the program, any text.

How to clear a finding

List the repository in the workspace file, or correct repo: in the slice file. Add the producer and the consumer to the contract.

The failure it prevents

A slice is planned for a repository the graph never walks, or a contract has no named consumer, so impact reports that a change to the interface affects nobody.
